entities.name: Abílio Rodas de Sousa Ribas
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abílio Rodas de Sousa Ribas (1934–2010) was a Portuguese-born Catholic bishop who served in Mozambique, bridging the colonial and post-independence eras of the Church in southeastern Africa. Ordained a priest in Portugal, he was appointed to episcopal ministry in Mozambique and served there through the country's independence from Portugal in 1975 and the subsequent civil war.

His episcopate spanned one of the most turbulent periods in Mozambican history, including the transition from colonial rule, the Marxist-Leninist single-party state under Frelimo, and the brutal civil war between Frelimo and Renamo that killed hundreds of thousands. During this period the Catholic Church in Mozambique navigated a complicated relationship with a government initially hostile to religious institutions, before gradually finding space for pastoral and social work.

Sousa Ribas contributed to the Church's efforts to maintain schools, health services, and sacramental life in conditions of extreme hardship. He retired in the 1990s as Mozambique moved toward democratic elections and the peace settlement that ended the civil war. His career embodied the larger story of Portuguese-speaking African Catholicism adapting from colonial institution to genuinely local Church.
